text: Mantis shrimp versus a snail shell.
Armor against a fist. Who wins?
The peacock mantis shrimp is only about the length of a pencil.
But it has two clubs folded under its body, like a boxer's fists.
A spring in its arm stores up energy. Then it lets go.
The club hits at up to twenty three meters per second. Around eighty kilometers an hour. Underwater.
Scientists needed a camera filming five thousand frames a second just to see it.
And the snail gets hit twice.
Then by a bubble. The strike is so fast it rips the water open, and that bubble collapses in a second blow.
It keeps striking until the shell gives way.
Its club is so tough that engineers study it to design stronger materials.
